75WX: Lal = O beloved! Na jana = I do not know.
O my beautiful Lord! I cannot know the limit of your qualities (I cannot understand how many excellences there are in you).
O my Dear Beloved Lord, Your limits are not known.
O my venerable beloved, I know not Your limit.
O my beloved ji! You are (samana) pervading within all.
7Z2A: Jal = in the water. Thal = within the earth. Maheeal = mahee tal, upon the surface of the earth, in the open space, in the sky. Bharipur = brimful. Leena = pervading. Ape = himself alone. ||1|| Rahau ||
You are brimful in the water, you are pervading within the earth, you are present everywhere in the sky, you yourself are contained within all beings and in all places. ||1|| Rahau ||
You pervade the water, the land, and the sky; You Yourself are All-pervading. ||1||Pause||
You are fully contained in water, dry land nether and upper regions. You Yourself are pervading everywhere. Pause.

My beloved, you are (bharipoor) full and mingled in the places of water, in the earth and in the sky; you yourself are (samana) contained in all forms, subtle and gross, inert and conscious. ||1|| Rahau ||
TKGT: Taraji = the scales. Teri sev kamava = may I do your service, may I remember you.

O Lord! If my mind were to become the scales, if my consciousness were to become the weight for weighing, if I could do your service, could remember you (if this service and remembrance were to become for me) the assayer,
Mind is the scale, consciousness the weights, and the performance of Your service is the appraiser.
My soul is the scale, the consciousness the weights and the performance of Your service is my jeweler.
O Bhagvan! If a pure mind be the scales and the consciousness be the weight, let me earn your service, (saraf) understanding this very thing.
GFYP: Ghat = the heart. Bheetar = within. Sahu = the husband-Lord. Toli = may I weigh, may I assay. Inh bidh = by these means. Rahava = may I hold. ||2||

(I shall not be able to find the limit of your qualities, but) by these means I shall be able to keep my consciousness fixed at your feet. (O brother!) I shall be able to assay that husband-Lord seated within my own heart. ||2||
Deep within my heart, I weigh my Husband Lord; in this way I focus my consciousness. ||2||
Within my mind I weigh the spouse, In this way I fix my attention.

In this way, within the inner self alone, (sahu) the husband, who is your form of sat, chit and anand — (so) whoever has (toli) reflected upon him in this way, then may I become one with you. ||2|| ☬ He shows the certainty of those who have become one with him:
KPWU: Kanda = the needle in the middle of the beam of the scales, the pointer of the scales.

(O brother! The Lord pervades every place; he himself alone knows his own greatness and can assay it) he himself is the scales, he is the weight of the scales, he is the pointer of the scales, and he himself is the one who weighs (his own qualities).
You Yourself are the balance, the weights and the scale; You Yourself are the weigher.
You Yourself are the tongue of the balance, the weights and the balance. You Yourself are the weighman.

You yourself are (kanda) the form of love, (tol) you yourself are the weight that is reflection, and you yourself are the scales that are the intellect; you yourself are (tolanhar) the one who reflects.
PJSY: Dekhai = he takes care. Boojhai = he understands. Vanjara = the trading soul-merchant. ||3||
He himself takes care of all beings, he himself understands the hearts of all, he himself, becoming the being, is carrying on the trade (of the Name) in the world. ||3||
You Yourself see, and You Yourself understand; You Yourself are the trader. ||3||
You Yourself beholdest, Yourself You understandest and You Yourself are the Dealer.

You yourself see the deeds and you yourself understand their fruit too, and (vanjara) the Sikh is also yourself; the meaning being that the seeker, the means and the Guru are all yourself alone. ||3||
3B47: Andhula = blind. Neech jat = of low caste. Pardesi = one who goes on wandering. Khin = in the time of the blinking of an eye. Til = in the least span of time.

That which is lying blind (in the attachment of Maya), which has become of low caste (with the filth of the vices of countless births), which goes on wandering for ever, which cannot stay in one place even for the least moment —
The blind, low class wandering soul, comes for a moment, and departs in an instant.
The blind of low caste, and the stranger soul comes but for a moment and departs in a trice.

O Parmesvar! My mind comes in a moment with its resolves and goes in the least instant; it is blind, and it (jat) brings forth those very resolves that are low; or, from the sattva portion of the five low elements that are not the self, the birth of this mind has come about. And, forsaking the state of the self, it has become the master of (pardesi) the country that is not the self.
KGTQ: Ta ki = of such a (mind). Kiau kar = in what way? Moora = the fool. Pavai = can find (its worth). ||4||2||9||
Nanak's company is ever with that mind, and because of it the ignorant Nanak cannot find the worth of the Lord's qualities. ||4||2||9||
In its company, Nanak dwells; how can the fool attain the Lord? ||4||2||9||
In its companionship Nanak abides. How can he, the fool, attain to You, O Lord?

Sri Guru ji says: I, your servant, remain in its company — the meaning being that I go under the sway of such a mind. (Kiau kar) in what way may the company of this foolish mind be removed, and may this servant attain you? ||4||2||9|| ☬ Instruction addressed to the mind:
